Order 21/07/2023 The present application for anticipatory bail under Section 438 Cr.P.C. has been
preferred on behalf of the petitioners who are apprehending their arrest in connection with F.I.R.
No.113/2023, registered at Police Station Lohawat, District Jodhpur Rural, for the offences under
Sections 376(D), 366, 328, 342 & 323 Ipc.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in a criminal case.

Learned counsel submitted that petitioner No.1 and prosecutrix (2 of 3)
[CRLMB-6817/2023] were having a love relationship.
However, parents of the prosecutrix were against the relationship.
Learned counsel further submitted that on 26.02.2023, prosecutrix out of her free will and volition married petitioner No.1 and they resided as a couple at Nagpur and Varda.

Learned counsel submitted that family members of the prosecutrix forcibly took her away from the company of present petitioner and brought her to Lohawat, Jodhpur, whereupon under the pressure of family members, the prosecutrix has roped the present petitioners in a false criminal case under Sections 376 and 366 IPC.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that in view of the fact that Rawal Bharat Lal Jajda vs State Of Rajasthan on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2066306/
1 prosecutrix is wife of petitioner No.1, the petitioners deserve to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail application and submitted that the allegation against the present petitioners is that on 22.02.2023, petitioner No.1 forced the prosecutrix to consume a drink containing intoxicant, due to which she became sedated, and was kidnapped by the petitioner No.1.
Learned Public Prosecutor submitted that thereafter, signatures of the prosecutrix were obtained on blank papers and her obscene photographs were also captured.
It was jointly submitted that the prosecutrix was subjected to forcible sexual assault by the petitioner and co- accused persons.
It was further submitted that the prosecutrix on 06.03.2023 with the help of her family members escaped from the clutches of the petitioners.
] Lastly, learned Public Prosecutor submitted that investigation in the matter is pending, therefore, the petitioners do not deserve to be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
Learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant jointly prayed that application for anticipatory bail may be rejected.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and upon a consideration of the arguments advanced at bar, this Court is of the prima facie opinion that there are serious allegations against the petitioners and the investigation in the matter is not yet completed.

In view of the aforesaid, no case for indulgence under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is made out and hence,
the instant application seeking anticipatory bail stands rejected.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 314-Prashant/-
